fixed_upstream.relevant_behavior: The fixed upstream pauses the active macro while a client screen is present, stops movement in its client tick guard, and resumes through the explicit MacroHandler lifecycle boundary. The modern 26.1.2 client has no equivalent downstream screen event adapter in the fixed upstream.

modern_client_boundary.replacement: MinecraftSetScreenMixin forwards the authoritative post-mutation setScreen boundary to a shared ClientScreenLifecycleAdapter. The adapter shares ClientSnapshotCapture identity state with the tick fallback, emits SCREEN_OPEN for non-chat present-screen transitions, and leaves only the exact command-armed chat close exempt. SCREEN_OPEN terminal fanout stops macro, desync, inventory, navigation, rotation, and managed input ownership; settings save is therefore allowed only after the macro is stopped.

findings.summary: A real non-chat Minecraft#setScreen transition did not reach a terminal client ownership boundary, leaving the SCREEN_OPEN macro lease stale after inventory and Escape pause flows.
findings.upstream_behavior: Fixed upstream keeps the macro out of its active tick path while a screen is present and exposes explicit pause/resume lifecycle operations. Its GUI container draw hook is a screen-adjacent integration point, not a modern Minecraft 26.1.2 setScreen lifecycle boundary.
findings.incompatibility: The current-master client observed screen state from the normal tick path and routed screen identity changes through SCREEN_CHANGED. The runtime deliberately preserves macro state for SCREEN_CHANGED, so the authoritative setScreen transition did not revoke terminal ownership. The parent R4 captures then showed no active rotation and no held input while enabled=true, state=paused, and pauses=[SCREEN_OPEN].
findings.replacement: Inject at the exact mapped Minecraft#setScreen(Screen) TAIL, forward the post-mutation client-thread state through one shared adapter, and retain the tick snapshot as a deduplicated fallback. Emit SCREEN_OPEN for every non-chat present-screen boundary, map it to terminal stop and ownership cleanup, and preserve only the exact command-armed chat close as a lease-preserving transition. Repeated identities and repeated closes remain idempotent.
